required_evidence: Prove the existence of one family of G-equivariant sections satisfying every transition equation under the actual arbitrary-characteristic field hypotheses.
Construct the stated equivariant direct-sum isomorphism at the inverse limit and verify its compatibility with i_infinity and q_infinity.
Classify all coherent sections, for example as a nonempty affine space under lim Hom_G(C,A_n), equivalently Hom_G(C,A_infinity), and verify their transport under isomorphisms of the whole tower.
critical_errors: Treat arbitrary independently chosen row sections as already coherent.
Assume the transition maps of modules or of section spaces are surjective; the hypotheses do not say this and the reference supplies a counterexample.
Invoke finiteness of G to divide by |G| in an arbitrary field.
Treat a finite-dimensional vector or affine space over an arbitrary field as a finite set or as a compact space without additional structure.
Assert a nonempty inverse limit of arbitrary nonempty sets without justifying a valid stabilization, compactness or algebraic-solvability argument.
Use the old nonsplit modular representation as a counterexample despite the new explicit assumption that every row admits an equivariant section.
Claim uniqueness of all coherent sections without excluding nonzero compatible equivariant kernel maps, or claim that a naturally transported solution space supplies a natural preferred section.
completion_policy: Complete the coherent existence, compatible limit decomposition and full solution-space transport requested in the task. Any correct short Mittag-Leffler, linear-algebraic compactness or equivalent argument is fully acceptable; no named theorem or author lemma sequence is mandatory. Finite dimensionality must enter some justified step unless the candidate proves an applicable stronger theorem. No optimal algorithm, uniform stabilization bound, averaging formula, obstruction class or natural preferred section is requested.
open_task_policy: Accept every independently verified proof or counterexample within the actual hypotheses. Do not require the author route, vocabulary, length, optional examples or conditional results. Explicit added-assumption results are valid separate contributions; silently treating them as completion of the original task is not. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
